sections.title: Tree and leaves
sections.text: Rhus typhina, staghorn sumac, is a deciduous, often suckering shrub or small tree, typically about 4.5–7.5 m tall and broad. Its large pinnate leaves bear many sharply toothed leaflets; young branches are densely velvety.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small greenish flowers form upright terminal clusters. The female clusters develop into conspicuous, upright cones of densely packed red, hairy drupes that persist into winter.

sections.title: Fruit use
sections.text: North American accounts describe the sour covering of the drupes as a traditional ingredient for a tart drink. The fruit is not the culinary spice sold as ground Middle Eastern sumac, which typically comes from other species; do not confuse staghorn sumac with poisonous lookalikes.
